newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end slightly up, led by Samsung Elec.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end slightly up, led by Samsung Elec.

text.p: The stock market managed to stay in positive territory by the end of Monday's trading despite profit-taking that cut its afternoon mini-rally, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed up 0.83 point to a provisional 769.20 as 28.48 million shares changed hands.
"Large-cap shares led the trading, while low-cap cheap shares which rose in the past several days underperformed the market," said Richard Kim of KLB Securities.
Samsung Electronics ended up 600 won to 58,900. Brokers said local investors were preparing for October 1 when the foreign shareholding ceiling will expand to 20 percent from 18 percent.
They added that the market was expected to gain a bit ahead of the expansion, forecasting the market could test the 800 level by next Tuesday.
LG Electronics, which had risen on Samsung's lead, ended flat at 13,100. Daewoo Heavy, which is seen as being oversold, saw active buying. It gained 340 to 6,090.

Individual shares backed by specific themes was also in the spotlight. Cable television-linked Dae Ho Construction and Midopa dominated the day's trading volume. Dae Ho rose 2,100 won to 38,300. Midopa rose 800 won to 14,500. Both companies own local cable operators in Seoul.

Brokers said the ongoing North Korean infiltration drama was not having a significant impact on the market, as foreign investors already calculate the risks of North-South tension before putting money into the market.

A North Korean submarine ran aground close to the east cost city of Kangnung last Wednesday. The vessel carried an estimated 26 Northern agents. So far 20 agents have been confirmed dead and one captured alive.
The December futures contract ended down 0.30 point to 80.50, while the KOSPI-200 index closed up 0.13 point to 80.33
